sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: PCT Patent Application and International Trademark Registration

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Mainland China (target WFOE registered seat; source investor jurisdiction: Taiwan)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: There is no bilateral investment treaty between mainland China and Taiwan because Taiwan is not a sovereign state; the applicable active cross-strait instruments are: Cross-Strait Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA) (2010)
Cross-Strait Agreement on Intellectual Property Rights Protection and Cooperation (2010)

Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation and Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income (signed 2015, applied in accordance with the respective domestic procedures of the mainland and Taiwan sides)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China, as revised on November 8, 2024 and effective January 1, 2025; Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information of Market Entities (State Administration for Market Regulation and People's Bank of China Order No. 3, effective November 1, 2024); Administrative Measures for Enterprise Name Registration (SAMR Order No. 45, effective March 1, 2021); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective January 1, 2020); Special Administrative Measures (Negative List) for Foreign Investment Access (2024 Edition); Patent Law of the People's Republic of China; Patent Agency Regulations of the People's Republic of China; and, for cross-strait document authentication, the Cross-Strait Agreement on Intellectual Property Rights Protection and Cooperation (2010).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Taiwan Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Company Registration Division, Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization path (Hague Apostille not applicable because Taiwan is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention): handle notarization before a Taiwan court notary, then verify the notarized copy through the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) and the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS), then present the verified document to the mainland SAMR and relevant notary associations; do not apply a Hague Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Company Registry Extract with Current Directors and UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Commercial Administration Office, Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization path (Hague Apostille not applicable): notarize the registry extract before a Taiwan court notary, transmit to SEF for authenticity verification, have ARATS verify the SEF seal, then file with the mainland Market Regulatory Administration and banks; use only the consular/cross-strait verification route, never a Hague Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for WFOE Formation and Banking Signatory Mandate
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Taiwan Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization path (Hague Apostille not applicable): sign the board resolution and power of attorney before the Taiwan board members, notarize signatures before a Taiwan court notary, verify through SEF and ARATS, then submit the verified Chinese translation to the relevant mainland authorities; do not chain with Apostille certification.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Memorandum and Articles) of the Taiwan Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan Corporate Shareholder as filed with the Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization path (Hague Apostille not applicable): take certified copies of the filed Articles of Association to a Taiwan court notary for notarization, proceed through SEF/ARATS cross-strait verification, then use the verified document for UBO piercing and name clearance in mainland China; no Apostille step is available or required.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the Taiwan Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan-licensed bank maintaining the corporate shareholder's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization path (Hague Apostille not applicable): the bank's authorized signatory must sign the reference letter before a Taiwan court notary, the notary certificate is verified by SEF and ARATS, and the verified letter accompanies the WFOE application and bank account onboarding package; the letter is not apostilled.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The mandatory screening protocol requires identification of every individual with direct or indirect ownership of 25% or more, all directors, legal representatives, ultimate beneficial owners, attorneys-in-fact, and designated customer contacts. Automated name-matching must be run against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU and UK consolidated sanctions, PRC Foreign Ministry and MOFCOM sanctions designations, and Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act designations. The compliance team must determine whether any UBO or authorized signatory qualifies as a politically exposed person (PEP) or a close associate thereof. All positive, fuzzy, or unresolved hits must be escalated through independent second-person review, documented, and retained. Source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence must be obtained for any PEP, prominent public function holder, or non-standard relationship. Screening evidence must be refreshed at signing and again immediately before name reservation and bank account onboarding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR Enterprise Name Registration and Pre-registration System (National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and provincial Market Regulatory Administration online service halls)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name must use standard simplified Chinese characters. English letters, Arabic numerals, including Roman numerals, and other non-Chinese characters are generally prohibited except where specifically approved by SAMR. The statutory four-tier structure is: administrative division + distinctive trade name + industry or business characteristic + company legal form. A foreign-invested enterprise may use a foreign-language trade name for external branding, but the Chinese registered name remains the sole statutory name. Phonetic transliteration of the Taiwan investor's trade name into Mandarin pinyin is permitted for the distinctive-name element, but the transliteration must be consistent, verifiable against the investor's certificate of incorporation, and must not duplicate an existing reserved name in the same registration authority.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon issuance of a name-rejection notice, the applicant or authorized agent must file a written appeal with the same Market Regulatory Administration within 15 working days of the electronic rejection, or with the immediate superior Market Regulatory Administration within 60 calendar days under the Administrative Reconsideration Law of the PRC. The appeal must identify the rejected name, state the alleged error of law or fact, submit at least three revised candidate names, and attach the rejection notice, UBO chart, Taiwan investor's certificate of incorporation, authenticated cross-strait documents, and signed board resolution. If administrative reconsideration is denied, the applicant may initiate an administrative lawsuit in the competent people's court within the statutory limitation period. All filings must be made through the SAMR online portal with stamped paper originals preserved.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible for this WFOE in the ISIC 7490 patent prosecution industry. The Market Regulatory Administration requires the registered office to be an actual leased or owned physical premises evidenced by a lease agreement and property ownership certificate. The local tax authority requires an operational fixed place of business for tax registration, fiscal invoice controls, and site inspections. The China National Intellectual Property Administration patent agency license requires fixed offices, full-time patent agents, and demonstrated commercial substance. Commercial banks reject virtual or desk-only addresses during AML KYC because the corporate account opening process includes an on-site visit by bank compliance officers. The WFOE should therefore secure a physical commercial office from the effective date of incorporation.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: HIGH, estimated at 75% likelihood of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 12 months for a licensed patent prosecution agency. Inspection checklist: original lease agreement and property ownership certificate; business license displayed at the premises; original company seals, statutory books, and bank ledgers available; at least one full-time licensed patent agent present during business hours; employee labor contracts and social insurance records maintained; fire-safety inspection certificate if applicable; and all CNIPA annual reporting documentation ready for immediate production.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official enterprise name pre-reservation and WFOE incorporation registration fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) / provincial Market Regulatory Administration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Abolished official fee; no statutory registry fee is currently charged by PRC SAMR for standard limited liability company incorporation filings.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Foreign investment information filing and negative-list compliance submission
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory government filing fee for a standard WFOE foreign investment information report; counsel time is billed separately.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company stamp engraving set (company chop, legal representative chop, financial seal, contract seal, invoice seal)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark in mainland China, typically USD 80 to USD 200 depending on stamp type and anti-forgery standard.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Taiwan shareholder corporate document notarization (certificate of incorporation, good standing extract, articles of association, board resolution, bank reference letter)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Taiwan statutory notary tariff plus prevailing notarial preparation charge for multiple-language corporate instruments.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Cross-strait SEF/ARATS verification fee and consular-legalization-equivalent handling
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) and Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing fixed inter-association notarial verification schedule for Taiwan-sourced documents used in mainland China.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Chinese translation and certification of all authenticated Taiwan corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translation provider and retained cross-border Chinese counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of RMB 80 to RMB 200 per page plus certification fee for notarially verified translation copies.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT pre-incorporation due diligence, UBO matrix construction, PEP and sanctions screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Retained cross-border corporate and AML/CFT law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for a single-matter UBO piercing and sanctions screening of a Taiwan-origin corporate investor into a PRC WFOE.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: WFOE articles of association drafting, incorporation resolutions, name-clearance strategy, and post-incorporation compliance checklist
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed-fee engagement per prevailing market benchmark for standard PRC WFOE formation with Taiwan-source authentication requirements.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: CNIPA patent agency license pre-incorporation advisory and commercial substance assessment
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Retained law firm and licensed PRC patent attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for regulatory eligibility review of ISIC 7490 patent prosecution agency under the Patent Agency Regulations of the PRC.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act, especially Articles 98 to 113 governing limited liability companies, Article 18 on company name protection, and Articles 19 to 21 on registration, read with the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals and the Patent Agent Act for professional licensing of patent prosecution activity.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Establishment Registration Application and Articles of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No general statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a limited company engaging in ISIC 7490 professional patent and trademark services; however the subscribed capital must be fully deposited in a Taiwan bank account and verified by a bank capital certificate before filing. Foreign capital remittance requires Investment Commission approval; no blocked escrow account is mandated for this non-financial service activity.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED at a duly convened first meeting of the board of directors of the Company held at the registered office upon notice to all founding directors and with the quorum lawfully present: (1) Approval of Articles: RESOLVED that the Company be and is hereby established as a limited company under the laws of Taiwan with the name appearing in Article 1 of the Articles of Incorporation and the principal business scope of professional patent prosecution services including PCT national phase entry, international trademark registration and related intellectual property consulting; that the form of Articles of Incorporation presented to this meeting be and is hereby adopted, ratified and confirmed as the constitutive instrument of the Company. (2) Share Capital: RESOLVED that the initial share capital of the Company as set out in the capital schedule is hereby duly subscribed by the shareholders whose names appear in the subscription register; that each shareholder shall pay the full amount of his or her respective subscription in immediately available funds into the designated capital account; that the receipt of such funds and the bank certificate of verification are hereby confirmed as the basis for registration. (3) Registered Office: RESOLVED that the address stated in Article 1 of the Articles of Incorporation is hereby adopted as the registered office of the Company and the President is authorized to sign the lease, utility service and any other agreements required for such office. (4) Banking: RESOLVED that the President and the Chief Financial Officer are jointly and severally authorized to open checking, savings, foreign currency and safety deposit accounts with a licensed commercial bank in Taiwan and to execute any banking forms and instruments, with any two of them authorized to draw, endorse and accept checks and electronic payment instructions. (5) Officers: RESOLVED that the General Manager, Company Secretary, Chief Financial Officer and Chief Compliance Officer are appointed as statutory officers of the Company with full authority to administer day-to-day operations, maintain corporate records, prepare tax filings and ensure regulatory compliance. (6) Regulatory Authorization: RESOLVED that the officers be and are hereby directed to prepare, execute and file all documents necessary for company registration, foreign investment registration, taxpayer registration, labour insurance registration and the patent agency license before the Taiwan Intellectual Property Office. (7) Effective Date: RESOLVED that this resolution is effective immediately and the Company shall indemnify each officer for good-faith actions taken pursuant to this resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval and Company Name Pre-Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan; online filing through the MOEA Company Registration One-Stop Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founding subscriber must submit the foreign investment application through the MOEA one-stop online system, stating the investment amount, shareholder structure, proposed business scope of ISIC 7490 professional patent prosecution and trademark registration services, and the planned registered capital. The applicant must upload the notarized passport or certificate of residence, bank references, a draft of the Articles of Incorporation, and an investment plan explaining the source of foreign funds. The Investment Commission will screen the application for national security, sensitive technology and sector restrictions. Once the approval letter is issued, the same portal reserves the company name and submits a preliminary review of the proposed company name and business scope to eliminate conflicts with registered trademarks or prohibited naming. Any required explanation must be filed within the statutory objection period; if the proposal is queried, the applicant may amend the proposed name and resubmit without an additional filing fee.
required_dossiers: Notarized proof of investor identity and residence
Bank reference and source of funds statement
Business plan including ISIC 7490 service scope
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended or issued with defective findings, the applicant may submit supplementary materials within 15 calendar days; if the refusal is administrative, the investor may file a petition for administrative review with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days of service of the refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of Paid-In Capital and Bank Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated licensed bank in Taiwan and the Investment Commission exchange-control desk for inbound remittance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the investment approval is granted, the founding subscriber opens a temporary share capital account in the Company's name at a licensed bank in Taiwan, remits the approved paid-in capital from overseas through an exchange settlement, and obtains a bank deposit certificate. The bank will verify that the remittance matches the approved investment amount, the foreign exchange settlement record and the subscriber's identity. The bank shall issue a capital verification certificate, which is a required filing document for company registration. For Taiwan dollar funds, the bank must issue a certificate of deposit balance; for foreign currencies, a bank statement converted at the exchange rate on remittance date. The funds cannot be withdrawn before the registration is completed unless directed by the Ministry of Economic Affairs for correction of defects. Ensure that source of funds documentation is retained and stamped by the remitting bank for anti-money laundering compliance.
required_dossiers: Capital verification certificate issued by Taiwan bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays verification due to currency mismatch, resubmit the corrected remittance and a revised foreign exchange settlement certificate; if a discrepancy persists, apply to the central bank foreign exchange department for reconciliation before resubmitting to the Ministry of Economic Affairs.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Documents and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public office in the competent Taiwan district; foreign documents may require legalization through the Taiwan overseas mission in the investor's home country
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The board members and shareholders execute the Articles of Incorporation, share subscription register, first board meeting minutes, and the registered office consent form from the lessor. All documents must be notarized before a Taiwan notary public if executed in Taiwan, or legalized through the Taiwan representative office in the investor's home country if executed abroad. The notary verifies the identities of signatories, the legal capacity of the corporate shareholder, and that the resolutions of the foreign investor's board were duly adopted. The notarized documents then become admissible evidence and are the official versions submitted to the company registration authority. The cost is borne by the Company; original and duplicate sets must be produced in Chinese or accompanied by authorized English translations.
required_dossiers: Share subscription and paid-in capital register
Consent letter of registered office owner
Notarized certificates of lawful authority for corporate subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization is rejected due to incomplete corporate authorization, require the foreign parent company's board resolution to be re-executed and legalized, then resubmit within 10 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration at MOEA Department of Commerce
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan; online portal: Company Registration Information System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company representative or an authorized incorporation agent files the Company Incorporation Registration Application together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation, capital verification certificate, foreign investment approval letter, registered office consent, identification documents, and the registration fee payment receipt. The Department of Commerce verifies the completeness of the filing, the legality of the business scope, the validity of the capital deposit, and compliance with the Company Act registration requirements. Upon approval, the authority issues the Company Incorporation Certificate and the company establishment stamp. The Company becomes a separate legal entity with limited liability on the date of registration. The representative must check that all officer names and addresses are correctly entered, because the certificate is legal proof of corporate existence for bank and tax purposes. Any amendment to officers after registration shall require a filing to the same authority within 15 days.
required_dossiers: First board resolution and officer appointment forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a correction notice, the Company has 15 days from receipt to file the corrected text or explanation; failure to cure may result in refusal, which can be appealed by filing an administrative lawsuit in the Taipei High Administrative Court within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, Patent Agent Licensing, and Business Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Administration, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan; and Taiwan Intellectual Property Office, Ministry of Economic Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the incorporation certificate, the Company must apply to the National Taxation Administration for tax registration and uniform invoice approval using the incorporation certificate, bank account details, and expected monthly turnover statement. Simultaneously, the responsible patent agent must submit his or her Patent Agent Registration Certificate, employment contract, and a copy of the incorporation certificate to the Taiwan Intellectual Property Office for a practice license, permitting the Company to act as a PCT patent prosecution agency. The National Taxation Administration will issue a taxpayer identification number and approve the use of government-issued uniform invoices. The Taiwan Intellectual Property Office will verify the qualifications of the agent and the existence of a physical office. The Company must also complete labour and health insurance registration with the Bureau of Labor Insurance. For this non-manufacturing professional service, no industrial operating permit or environmental assessment is needed; however, a general fire safety and workplace self-inspection checklist should be retained.
required_dossiers: Tax registration and uniform invoice application
Bank details and capital verification certificate
Patent Agent Registration Certificate of the supervising agent
Office lease and physical site confirmation
Labour insurance and health insurance registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Taiwan Intellectual Property Office refuses license registration for lack of patent agent qualification, the Company may appoint another qualified licensed patent agent and refile; if tax registration is queried for turnover estimates, provide the business plan to the regional tax bureau and request reconsideration.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Taiwan Intellectual Property Office, Ministry of Economic Affairs; the Industrial Development Administration is not applicable because ISIC 7490 is a non-manufacturing professional service activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Patent Agency Registration Certificate and Taxpayer Registration Certificate; no industrial manufacturing operating permit is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration, Executive Yuan, Taiwan
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt and Not Applicable because ISIC 7490 is a professional, non-manufacturing intellectual-property service activity that does not trigger the Environmental Impact Assessment Act; no project EIA, environmental registration, or public hearing is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable because the undertaking is office-based with no process wastewater, VOC emissions, combustion stack gases, or hazardous waste; only general municipal solid waste is generated and must be handled under local waste storage and clearance regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for heavy plant clearance; however, the office must maintain fire safety equipment and annual fire safety reporting compliance under the Fire Services Act, including extinguishers, alarm systems and evacuation signage, together with an occupational accident prevention plan under the Occupational Safety and Health Act and a general structural safety declaration for the leased office space.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, R.O.C. (Taiwan) and the regional National Taxation Bureau with jurisdiction over the registered branch address (e.g., National Taxation Bureau of Taipei, Ministry of Finance); online portal: Ministry of Finance Tax Entry Portal (eTax Portal) at https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw and e-Invoice Integration Service Platform at https://www.einvoice.nat.gov.tw
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Taiwan branch of a China-incorporated WFOE: (1) obtain inward investment approval from the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), under the regulations governing Mainland Area investor investments in Taiwan; (2) file the foreign company branch registration with the MOEA company registry, providing a Taiwanese head office manager and local registered address; (3) receive the statutory eight-digit Unified Business Number from the MOEA registry, which functions as both the corporate identifier and the tax/VAT identification number; (4) complete tax registration with the local National Taxation Bureau, establish taxpayer identity, and apply for a tax registration certificate; (5) register as an e-invoice issuer with the MOF e-Invoice Integration Service Platform if issuing electronic Uniform Invoices; and (6) appoint a Taiwan tax filing agent and file any required professional license coordination with the Taiwan Intellectual Property Office for patent agent services. The Unified Business Number is the evidence of TIN/VAT registration and must be included on all Uniform Invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Taiwan profit-seeking enterprise; branch of a foreign company is taxed at entity level on Taiwan-source income and is not a pass-through).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan income tax does not offer check-the-box pass-through or hybrid mismatch elections to a limited company or branch; the branch is mandatorily classified as a profit-seeking enterprise for corporate income tax and as a Business Tax registrant for VAT purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Taiwan Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax (Business Tax) - VAT-type indirect tax on goods and services
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a fixed-place-of-business branch: mandatory registration from the first day of operations, with no turnover threshold. For a small domestic business, the general threshold is NT$200,000 monthly taxable sales; for non-resident sellers of digital services occupying the Taiwan market, registration is triggered by annual taxable sales exceeding NT$480,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan requires VAT-registered businesses to issue Uniform Invoices for taxable sales. Authorized e-invoice issuers operate through the MOF e-Invoice Integration Service Platform by transmitting invoice data via web or Turnkey XML application interface; the platform validates the business number, invoice number, and aggregate data, and archives invoices for automated cross-checking with the periodic VAT return. Taiwan does not currently impose an invoice-by-invoice real-time fiscal counter-stamping or digital anti-fraud stamping module; controls are centralized invoice number allocation, controlled procurement of paper Uniform Invoices from authorized printing plants, encrypted Turnkey transmission, and electronic return matching.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Article 7 of the Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax Act zero-rates goods exported from Taiwan and services provided in Taiwan that are actually used or consumed outside Taiwan. For the PCT patent prosecution agency, the services must be supplied to a non-resident client and the substantive benefit/use of the service must occur outside Taiwan; services that support only Taiwan domestic filings remain taxable at 5%. The zero-rating must be evidenced by contemporaneous contracts, invoices, work product, and payment records.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Taiwan Customs Export Declaration (export declaration number and status) for any physical goods component
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing export movement from Taiwan
Commercial export invoice referencing the zero-rated Article 7 Business Tax classification
Foreign buyer purchase order or service contract identifying the non-resident client, place of performance, and place of use
Bank foreign exchange collection statement, inward remittance advice, or foreign exchange settlement receipt proving repatriation of export proceeds to Taiwan
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If zero-rating is claimed without the required export and exchange substantiation, the tax authority will claw back the 5% output tax and disallow the related input tax credits, adding interest from the original filing date. Under Article 51 of the Business Tax Act, underpayment may subject the taxpayer to a penalty of one to three times the underpaid tax; forged export documents, false invoices, or fraudulent refund claims can trigger higher evasion penalties, criminal referral, and extension of the tax assessment period under the Tax Collection Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) acting under the delegated authority of the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The People's Republic of China operates a managed float with substantial current account convertibility but strict capital account control. For the Taiwan-owned WFOE, current account transactions, including service fees for patent prosecution and IP licensing, are freely convertible upon submission of authentic commercial documents, tax vouchers, and customs declarations. Capital account items such as registered capital injection, shareholder loans, and overseas investment are not freely convertible; they require prior SAFE registration and are monitored through a dedicated capital account (FDI) at the bank. Profit remittances are permitted only after annual audits, tax clearance, and verification of retained earnings; the remittance is considered a current account item and is processed without a mandatory conversion surplus. Exchange surrender requirements have been relaxed over time, yet all foreign exchange receipts must be repatriated to a domestic SAFE-designated bank distance, although the enterprise may hold foreign currency or convert it voluntarily. Taiwan is a separate customs territory under the WTO framework, and all financial flows between Taiwan and mainland China are treated as cross-border, requiring cross-strait remittance documentation, enhanced due diligence, and additional compliance screening by the designated bank. As a result, a highly structured liquidity environment is in place where each capital flow must align with a registered commercial purpose and be supported by a closed loop of contractual, invoice, and payment evidence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For goods trade export proceeds, the WFOE must repatriate the full invoice amount to a domestic SAFE-designated bank within 90 days after the date of export declaration. For service trade including patent prosecution and IP licensing, proceeds must be repatriated according to the contractual payment schedule, but no later than the agreed settlement date. There is currently no mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds; the WFOE may freely retain foreign currency in its current account or sell it to the bank at the prevailing market rate. All receipts must be logged in the bank's foreign exchange monitoring system and reconciled against the customs, tax, and contract documentation. Any extended delay or non-repatriation without an approved extension will trigger a compliance inquiry and potential administrative penalty.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (FDI) and Basic Operational RMB Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Settlement Account (Basic Operational Current Account)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore fintech EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer, or Revolut Business are not licensed by SAFE or the PBOC to provide primary corporate bank accounts, hold client funds, or facilitate capital account transactions for a mainland Chinese WFOE. These platforms lack the statutory registration and custody framework required to receive FDI capital injections, verify export proceeds, or support SAFE-controlled current account conversions. They may be used only as ancillary non-bank payment channels for micro outbound disbursements outside the statutory banking system, but even then, legal risk remains because all cross-border trade settlement must flow through a SAFE-designated bank. Therefore, the overall viability rating for using any fintech EMI as the main treasury rail is Low, and the treasury blueprint must rely exclusively on Tier-1 domestic commercial banks for all regulated FX and clearing activity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under current cross-strait banking rules, the legal representative and at least one statutory director of the WFOE must be physically present at the designated branch to open the foreign exchange capital account and complete the face-to-face interview with the bank’s compliance officer. Remote or consular proxy opening is not accepted for the first foreign exchange account activation unless a notarized power of attorney is executed in Taiwan and verified through the Cross-Strait Notarization and Verification Exchange; however, the final sign-off still requires a bank officer to conduct an independent telephone or video verification with the principal, and a physical branch visit is generally mandatory for the signatory. For the basic RMB settlement account, physical presence may be waived after the initial risk-based review if the bank has established a dedicated cross-strait client desk with pre-existing relationship records, but the statutory capital account cannot be activated without an in-person interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction indicator: Taiwan is not categorised as a high-risk jurisdiction, but the cross-strait relationship triggers an Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) flag due to potential round-tripping of mainland Chinese funds through Taiwanese shell entities.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised Taiwan company registry and certificate of incorporation issued by the Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs; audited financial statements of the Taiwan investor for the prior three years; bank statements of the Taiwan investor for the last twelve months showing the source of funds; an affidavit from the ultimate beneficial owner explaining the purpose of the WFOE and the commercial nexus between the mainland business and the Taiwanese parent; a written declaration that no PRC tax-resident individual or entity holds a direct or indirect beneficial interest in the Taiwanese investor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Significant jump in patent prosecution service fees compared to industry peers, creating a trade-based money laundering red flag via inflated IP royalty or service invoicing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete set of signed client engagement agreements detailing the fee schedule; a patent prosecution docket showing the exact number of filed applications, office actions, and official fee receipts from patent offices such as USPTO, EPO, CNIPA, or JPO; valuation of value-added services such as search reports, technical translations, and legal opinions; a third-party benchmark study or IP valuation report confirming the market reasonableness of the fees charged.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The WFOE’s registered capital is being injected in non-cash assets, such as patent rights or trademarks, or through multiple small-value transfers structured to avoid mandatory large-amount reporting thresholds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE-approved foreign exchange registration form for the FDI; deferred capital contribution schedule filed with the local commerce authority; title deeds, patent registration certificates, and audited valuation reports supporting any in-kind capital contribution; complete SWIFT transfer records containing the SAFE registration reference and the explicit purpose code for FDI equity injection, along with a statement of capital verification issued by a certified public accountant.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The ultimate beneficial owner appears on a sanctions or politically exposed persons (PEP) list, or holds more than 25% of a conglomerate with sanctioned operations or litigation exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Reputable database screening results (e.g., Dow Jones, World-Check) dated within ninety days; an authoritative legal opinion or certification confirming no sanctions or PEP nexus; source-of-wealth evidence derived from declared professional income and asset statements; a personal career history with references; a Taiwanese resident identification certificate and a police clearance certificate issued by the Taiwan police authority.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must route via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 through a designated SAFE-approved bank in mainland China. The remitter in Taiwan must include the SAFE registration certificate number and the appropriate purpose code for foreign direct investment equity injection in the payment narrative of the wire transfer. The WFOE must complete the FDI filing with the local SAFE branch before the capital transfer is initiated. Once the funds arrive in the foreign exchange capital account, the amount is blocked until a certified public accountant provides a capital verification statement. After capital verification, funds may be transferred to the RMB basic settlement account for operational deployment under the 'payment after confirmation' regime, which requires that each disbursement be matched against the approved business scope of the WFOE. Any misuse of capital account funds is treated as a severe compliance violation and may result in fines under PRC foreign exchange regulations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For patent office fees, translation costs, and foreign legal services, the preferred clearing rail is a direct SWIFT MT103 message initiated from the WFOE’s domestic bank to the beneficiary’s bank, carrying the proper current account purpose code for professional and legal services or royalties and license fees. For high-value annual multi-jurisdiction PCT portfolio settlements, the WFOE may instruct its bank to issue a Commercial Letter of Credit through a confirming bank, or to arrange a Documentary Collection. Because the business is service-oriented, open account settlement with electronic invoice reconciliation is acceptable for low-risk counterparties; however, official patent office fees must be remitted to the designated official bank account of each patent office or settled through the patent office’s electronic payment gateway using the national payment reference. All outbound payments must be supported by the underlying service contract, the tax certificate for withholding where applicable, and a detailed invoice or fee schedule to satisfy SAFE’s current account audit trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts with a domestic SAFE-designated bank, used to hedge USD, TWD, or EUR receivable and payable exposures arising from service fees and patent office disbursements, provided the underlying transaction is genuine and the settlement is backed by commercial documentation.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps and FX swaps for longer-dated exposures, subject to demonstrated hedging need and annual SAFE registration where the notional exceeds the voluntary filing threshold.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are generally not permissible for onshore WFOE entities outside a Free Trade Zone account framework; even within a FTZ, explicit SAFE authorization is required, and such authorisation is rarely granted to patent prosecution agencies. Therefore, the treasury blueprint does not include NDFs as a standard hedging instrument.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Operations Report under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March immediately after the close of each calendar fiscal year (within 3 months of fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a formal correction order, administrative fine, and suspension of future foreign-investment applications; persistent non-filing can result in revocation of the foreign-investment approval and administrative strike-off of the WFOE registration by the Ministry of Economic Affairs.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Settlement Return and Full Tax Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (local district tax bureau)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed and paid from 1 May to 31 May of each year for the prior calendar fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty accrues at 3% of the unpaid tax for every two days of delay, capped at 15%; delayed payment interest is charged monthly; if the return is not filed after a demand notice, an additional 20% penalty and asset seizure can follow, and chronic non-compliance may lead to compulsory dissolution and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Bi-Monthly Business Tax / VAT Return (Uniform Invoice filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the 15th day of the month following every two-month VAT period; 6 filings per annual cycle (Jan-Feb, Mar-Apr, May-Jun, Jul-Aug, Sep-Oct, Nov-Dec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 1% for every two days of delay, capped at 15% of the payable tax; late-payment interest is imposed; repeated non-filing can cause revocation of tax registration and consequent administrative strike-off of the business license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements, Business Report and Shareholders Meeting Approval Package (Company Act Article 20 and 230 Compliance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs Company Registration Office and retained statutory records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Financial statements must be approved by the shareholders meeting no later than 30 June for a calendar-year company; the statutory filing and shareholder minutes must be submitted to MOEA within 30 days after approval, and in any event no later than 31 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare, approve, or file the required statements and minutes exposes the WFOE to administrative fines of NT$10,000 to NT$50,000 per non-compliant item; continued default after a final correction order will result in administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership and Substantial Shareholder Annual Confirmation / Change Report under Company Act Article 22-1
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs Company Registration and Information Platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation must be submitted by 31 January following each fiscal year; any shareholding transfer, change of ultimate controller, or change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 15 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or false declaration of beneficial ownership carries fines of NT$50,000 to NT$500,000, plus potential daily continuing fines; prolonged non-compliance after warning is an administrative strike-off trigger.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Patent Prosecution Agency Practice Declaration and Licensed Practitioner Registry Verification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Taiwan Intellectual Property Office (TIPO), Ministry of Economic Affairs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 January each year or as stated on the annual practice verification notice issued by TIPO
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Operating the patent prosecution agency without an active licensed patent practitioner or failing the annual practice declaration results in administrative penalties, suspension of client work, revocation of the professional license, and administrative strike-off of the business registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Taiwan WFOE is legally required to engage an independent licensed CPA for a full statutory audit if any of the following quantitative thresholds is exceeded: (a) paid-in capital exceeds NT$30 million (approx. USD 1.0 million); (b) annual operating revenue exceeds NT$50 million (approx. USD 1.65 million); (c) balance-sheet total assets exceed NT$150 million (approx. USD 5.0 million); (d) the average annual headcount exceeds 100 employees, bringing the entity within MOEA substantial-enterprise guidance; or (e) the statutory licensing authority (TIPO for patent prosecution) or the Investment Commission imposes CPA certification as a condition of license or foreign-investment approval. If any threshold is met, the audit must be performed by an independent CPA registered with the Taiwan CPA Association and the audited financial statements must be submitted to the Investment Commission, the tax authority, and the MOEA as required.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Mandatory-audit WFOEs must report under Taiwan International Financial Reporting Standards (TIFRS) as adopted by the Financial Supervisory Commission; private SMEs not otherwise required may use ROC Enterprise Accounting Standards (EAS/SME GAAP). All audited financial statements must be expressed in New Taiwan Dollars and may be accompanied by an English convenience translation for foreign shareholders.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Company Act Article 22-1 and the AML regime, the WFOE must maintain a beneficial owner register at its registered office and file any change in beneficial ownership or shareholding transfer with the MOEA company registry within 15 days of the event; the annual UBO confirmation must be performed and submitted by 31 January each year, including a zero-confirmation when no ownership change has occurred. The 30-day shareholder-transfer reconciliation window is also observed as the maximum internal book-closing period, but the statutory MOEA alteration filing must be completed within 15 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficial Owners / Substantial Shareholders

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - 1,800 per year for registered office, corporate secretarial agent and statutory representation in Taipei.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - 8,000 per year for a full CPA statutory audit of a licensed IP patent prosecution WFOE; USD 1,800 - 3,500 per year if only a review-level CPA engagement is required because the company remains below the mandatory audit thresholds.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying WFOEs can access investment tax credits, an R&D expenditure credit equal to 15% of incremental R&D spending (capped at 20% of income tax payable), and a 5-year tax holiday for newly established innovative industries. However, free-zone and offshore IP holding incentives may be restricted for PCT patent prosecution agencies unless substantive activity is performed in Taiwan.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 15 - Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return, filed electronically via the Taiwan Taxation and Customs Administration e-Filing System (TaxWeb / online declaration platform)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be filed no later than 5 months after the end of the fiscal year (calendar-year WFOEs must file by 31 May of the following year), together with the financial statements, shareholders' meeting resolution or book-entry income appropriation schedule, and audited reports.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the company name, tax identification number, date of incorporation, business address, and fiscal year period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For CN_WFOE_LTD, use the Taiwan commercial registration certificate as the basis. Attach the cross-strait investment approval reference number. Confirm whether the entity elects to be taxed as a resident profit-seeking enterprise; non-resident branch status would require a different return and rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicate the principal business service code and give a short description of the business.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use ISIC 7490 / NAICS 541199. The patent prosecution agency must note the scope as PCT patent filing and international trademark registration; this directly affects revenue classification and any service-related expense deductions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare total gross service revenue, including all Taiwan-source fees for patent preparation, filing, prosecution, and trademark registration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If fees are paid by the CN parent or non-resident clients, ensure they are allocated as Taiwan-source service revenue because the personal performing services and enforcement activity takes place in Taiwan. Exclude any intercompany dividends or capital contributions. Keep the Wise and Official Patent Office wire payment rails separately documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report direct labor and directly attributable expenses for patent attorneys, claim drafting, search fees, official filing fees, and translation costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reimburse only actual outgoing patent office fees; intercompany charges with the CN parent must satisfy the arm's length principle and be supported by purchase orders and invoices. Avoid deducting excessive management fees that create an artificial loss.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare general administrative expenses, rent, salaries, utilities, insurance, and professional expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE makes cross-border payments to non-resident service providers, report the items under gross payable amounts subject to WHT rates of 20% for fees; if the non-resident is the CN parent, notional WHT must be applied in accordance with the cross-strait tax protocol until a treaty relief approval is obtained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating profit computed as gross revenue less direct costs and operating expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Make any section 39 loss carryforward adjustments and adjust for permanent/temporary differences. The net income figure is the starting point for AMT and retained earnings surtax computations. A large unexplained loss at the CN_WFOE_LTD entity when the underlying patent business is profitable will trigger transfer pricing audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Transfer Pricing Declaration and Attachments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complete the required TP declaration embedded in the tax return, indicating whether related party transactions exceed the statutory threshold and whether a Local File and Master File have been prepared.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For intercompany transactions with the CN parent exceeding NT$200 million, attach a detailed TP report and disclose the selected arm's length method (TNMM, CUP, etc.). Failure to complete this box accurately constitutes a false statement and may lead to penalty under Article 110.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Withholding Tax and Credits (prepaid and refundable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare the aggregate tax withheld by domestic tax-withholding agents on business revenues (e.g., interest, government fees) and tax payments made by installments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE is treated as a resident, its non-resident parent is not entitled to claim these credits. However, the WFOE itself must claim any foreign tax credits on income sourced outside Taiwan, subject to foreign tax credit limit rules. Do not claim a DTA relief line without first obtaining and attaching the TRC from China.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a surcharge of 1% of the tax amount for every two days of default, capped at 10%, plus additional interest at the postal bank's one-year fixed-interest rate. Where the tax authority determines understatement, an administrative penalty of up to three times the underpaid amount is imposed under Income Tax Act Article 110. Fraudulently evading tax may be referred under Tax Collection Act Article 41, exposing directors to imprisonment up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% for non-resident profit-seeking enterprises (21% for non-resident individuals); an additional 5% retained earnings surtax applies to undistributed profits under Article 66-9 of the Income Tax Act.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a reduced DTA withholding rate on dividends, interest, or royalties, the CN parent must provide a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the Chinese tax authority (State Taxation Administration), a declaration of beneficial ownership (Form IA), and a Taiwan withholding agent application to the Ministry of Finance; the Taiwan payer must obtain an advance approval or otherwise meet the beneficial ownership test by demonstrating no conduit arrangement. In practice, cross-strait China-Taiwan double tax relief is limited: the Cross-Strait Taxation Agreement has a complex status, so advisors should confirm availability on a case-by-case basis.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties to non-residents are subject to 20% statutory WHT, unless reduced to nil, 10%, or 15% under a relevant DTA, depending on the treaty text and beneficial ownership. Interest to non-resident financial institutions or related companies is subject to 20% statutory WHT, and most Taiwanese DTAs reduce interest withholding to 10%; whether the CN parent can use the cross-strait arrangement requires tax authority confirmation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: NT$200 million in annual related-party transactions (approximately USD 6.7 million) generally triggers the mandatory preparation of Local File and Master File; for businesses operating at a loss or in certain designated industries the threshold can be lower.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan has no separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) code; however, the tax authority applies a real substance requirement in the actual management place test and in the practice under Taiwanese corporate and tax law. A patent prosecution agency claiming treaty benefits or preferential incentive regimes must maintain substantive economic presence in Taiwan, including permanent offices, qualified professionals, full-time staff, board meetings, and core IP prosecution decision-making (CIGA) physically taking place in Taiwan.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally suppressing service revenue from PCT patent filing and trademark registration work or fabricating a loss through inflated intercompany management fees paid to a related shell offshore IP company, thereby reducing Taiwan corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 110 of the Income Tax Act, an administrative penalty of up to three times the underpaid tax is imposed; Article 41 of the Tax Collection Act criminalizes the conduct with imprisonment for up to five years, detention, or a fine.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly signed or took part in the false return are personally liable to restore unpaid taxes, assets may be frozen, travel may be blocked under Article 24 of the Tax Collection Act if arrears exceed NT$2 million, and criminal imprisonment may be imposed for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare, retain, or timely submit Local File, Master File, Country-by-Country Report, or the annual transfer pricing disclosure when the intercompany transaction amount exceeds the NT$200 million statutory threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may disregard the taxpayer's structure, re-determine the arm's length profit using the most reasonable method, and impose a penalty of up to three times the understated tax amount; failure to submit required documentation may also trigger a separate fine.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the TP disclosure failure is deliberate and causes tax underpayment, directors can be held to have violated the tax law and become personally liable for underpaid taxes, interest, and penalties; they may also be blacklisted from leaving Taiwan and criminally prosecuted.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / DTA Abuse Without Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Relying on treaty or cross-strait reduced withholding rates without operating a real business in Taiwan, e.g., no physical office, no employees, no management functions, and no core income-generating activity performed in Taiwan, while characterizing patent prosecution fees as passive services routed through a conduit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty relief, re-characterization of the transaction as a sham, inclusion of the income in Taiwan corporate income, and an additional penalty of up to three times the evaded tax; serious cases are referred as tax fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable for the aggregate tax, interest, and penalties after piercing the corporate veil; personal travel bans, asset seizure, and imprisonment apply where the shell arrangement is proven fraudulent.
